key_insight: Lifting improves mid-circuit measurement reliability by combining repetition encoding, neural decoding, and in situ calibration to better discriminate quantum states under hardware noise.
engineering_relevance: It can strengthen error correction and outcome-dependent control on superconducting quantum processors by making readout more robust to noisy, changing execution conditions.
method: Encode measurements using joint I-Q signals from target and auxiliary qubits.
Train a neural decoder on contextual, in situ calibration data matched to execution conditions.
Leverage theory showing added channels from a fixed joint distribution do not increase Bayes risk.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated experimentally across three IBM processors on repeated stabilizer measurement, parity-check, and teleportation workloads.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on collecting reliable in situ calibration data and integrating extra readout channels without adding hardware or calibration overhead that outweighs the gains.
paper_title: Lifting: Quantum State Discrimination Framework for Mid-Circuit Measurements
